title: Beyond the 956: Mike 'Pancho' Locke, 'Dirty Sanchez' star, dies at 47
excerpt: Mike "Pancho" Locke, star of MTV's Dirty Sanchez, has died at 47. His family announced his death on Friday, November 6, 2026. The Welsh stuntman and skateboarder rose to fame on the outrageous MTV series that ran from 2003 to 2007.
content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Mike "Pancho" Locke, the Welsh stuntman and skateboarder who became a star of MTV's Dirty Sanchez, has died at 47.

His death was announced on Friday, November 6, 2026, in a statement shared by his family and his clothing brand, San Portablo, on Instagram. "It is with profound sadness that San Portablo and the Locke family write of the passing of the father, son, brother, uncle, friend, skater, stuntman and all-round goodfella Michael Richard Locke," the statement said, calling him "an absolute Welsh treasure." No cause of death was given, and the exact date of his death was not disclosed.

Born on March 13, 1979, in Neath, Wales, Locke was a professional skateboarder before finding fame on television. He shot to fame in 2003 on Dirty Sanchez, MTV's outrageous stunt and prank series, alongside Matthew Pritchard, Lee Dainton and Dan Joyce. Often described as the UK's answer to Jackass, the show ran for four series and 29 episodes through 2007, and drew tens of millions of viewers. Locke later appeared with Pritchard as the "Pain Men" on Channel 4's Balls of Steel.

After the show ended, Locke stayed rooted in his hometown area of Port Talbot, where he co-owned the streetwear brand San Portablo. He was a father of two. In interviews, he spoke openly about living with PTSD after years of performing extreme stunts.

Tributes poured in from his former co-stars. Matthew Pritchard shared an emotional video message while climbing in the Himalayas, saying his friend of 35 years had "left the building," and Lee Dainton said memories of their time together had been "flooding back."

Rest in Peace, Pancho.

Sources: Family statement via San Portablo; BBC News; WalesOnline; LADbible.
